pr.title: Plan project console, a terminal list of every live session that answers and discusses Claude Code and Codex items alike
pr.head: 30c424b729d43080259938a8e61bf9fb1656f734

summary: Projector’s inbox holds questions, requests, and notices that an agent posts for you. The existing Claude Code panel delivers your answers, but an idle Codex session needs another delivery path. This plan adds that path and a terminal console that opens each live session’s own panel.

The console records your choices while the session’s existing deliverer sends them. Item threads carry your discussion messages to the agent and show its replies in the console or Claude Code panel. This pull request contains the ready plan; the proposed commands and adapters remain to be implemented.

cards.title: Terms used in the plan
cards.html:
• Inbox item: a question, request, notice, or proposed discussion stored for one session.
  • Deliverer: the Claude Code panel or Codex adapter that sends an item’s line to its session.
  • Claim: the expiring token that lets one deliverer send a line at a time.
  • Thread: the ordered messages attached to an inbox item.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: The earlier readiness finding is fixed. The plan now defines how an empty session starts a discussion from the console or CLI, including its item shape and acceptance cases. The configured gate, exact-head CI, and project metadata checks passed.

groups.title: A console for each live session
groups.kicker: Delivery, discussions, terminal controls, and staged implementation
intro: The console first lists live sessions, then opens one session’s pull requests and inbox. Its recording calls always name that session, so answering an item or dismissing a pull request cannot affect another session’s copy.

For Codex, the watch adapter claims inbox lines, renews queued claims, and marks delivery after its batch is acknowledged. Discussion threads add ordered person messages and agent replies without making the console a second deliverer.

The plan also ports pull-request row rules to Python with shared fixtures for the existing TypeScript panel. Four dependent implementation changes separate delivery, threads, row parity, and the final console.

files.note: Defines the ready console plan, including inbox delivery, discussion storage, terminal interaction, acceptance criteria, and rollout.

checks.text: Section 2.2 keeps claims alive until Codex acknowledges the batch. Failed queue submissions retain the person’s answer, and disconnects let the claim expire for a later deliverer.

The earlier empty-session gap is fixed: pressing 7 with no drawer open starts a session discussion even when the panel has no rows. Section 2.6 also defines its targetless CLI form and item without a pull-request field; section 4 adds acceptance cases.

The review traced the complete delivery design against inbox claim/settle and Codex prepare/consume APIs. The gate and exact-head CI passed, including 237 hook tests; metadata checks confirm status ready and priority now.
Section 7 explicitly defers a combined item view, inactive-session items, Windows support, and future Codex UI surfaces. The session-only discussion path is specified in the current scope.
